clue.text: Franciscan mission not entirely fashionable

indicators.note: not entirely tells us to drop the closing letters of the phrase for fashionable

parts.note: fashionable is a la mode, written here as one run of letters

explanation.surface: A Franciscan mission that is somewhat out of vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts DE from ALAMODE (a la mode). The Alamo in Texas began as a Spanish Franciscan mission before its famous siege.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in San Antonio was founded as a Spanish mission run by Franciscan friars.

clue.text: Herb Hutton returned to the marsh

parts.note: a fen is a marsh

indicators.note: returned means the cricketer's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Len Hutton was a famous English cricket captain

explanation.surface: Someone named Hutton brings a herb back to the marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LEN to NEL. Sir Len Hutton was a great English batsman of the 1930s-50s, so the clue wants his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fennel is an aromatic plant of the carrot family used as a culinary herb.

clue.text: An insect mutation for example

indicators.note: a mutation is a change of form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mutated insect offered as a specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutation' rearranges AN INSECT; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or illustration offered to show something typical.

clue.text: Arrangement to admit us into the sports-ground

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters of the words are reordered

explanation.surface: Plans are made to let us into the sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' rearranges ADMIT plus US; 'to' and 'into the' are link words, and 'admit' looks like an instruction to insert but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium is a large venue with tiered seating where games are played.

clue.text: Flower produced despite poor drainage

indicators.note: poor suggests the word drainage is in bad shape and so reworked

explanation.surface: A flower blooms even though the soil drains badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges DRAINAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is a shrub with fragrant white blossoms.

clue.text: Fine sculpturing material results from a laboratory bloomer

parts.note: an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A precious carving stone emerges from a mistake made in a lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flower that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft translucent stone, a form of gypsum, prized for carving ornaments and statues.

clue.text: Take turns to change neat design

parts.note: to alter is to change

indicators.note: design means the word neat is reworked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: People rotate duties to redo a tidy pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges NEAT into NATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to do things one after another in rotation.

clue.text: It is not true a moral can be taught by it

definitions.text: It is not true a moral can be taught by it

parts.words: It is not true a moral can be taught by it
parts.note: a made-up story, such as one of Aesop's, that ends with a lesson

explanation.surface: Someone denies that ethics can be learned from something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a denial ('it is not true that...'), but it actually describes an untrue story that carries a moral.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short invented tale, often with animals, ending in a moral lesson.

clue.text: Thrilling, nothing, just a little flower

indicators.note: nothing but a little of the word means only a short run inside it is taken

explanation.surface: A tiny bloom gives no thrill at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword favourite: something that flows, so a stream, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a small brook, and a flowing stream is a 'flow-er'.

clue.text: Rose might arrange a date with men

indicators.note: might arrange says the letters could be set in another order

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose may set up a date with some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name or flower, but it is the past tense of rise. 'might arrange' rearranges A DATE and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanated means came forth or issued, as something that rose up from a source.

clue.text: A conference of tribesmen from Ibadan?

indicators.note: from, with the question mark, hints the word is made out of the letters of the Nigerian city

explanation.surface: A tribal meeting perhaps held in the Nigerian city of Ibadan.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is signalled only loosely by 'from' and the question mark: IBADAN rearranged. An indaba is a southern African council meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Indaba is a Zulu word for a council or meeting of tribal leaders to discuss affairs.

clue.text: Idea for softening top of flan

indicators.note: softening the top swaps the first letter, forte, for the musical sign for soft

explanation.surface: A suggestion to make the top of a flan less crisp.
explanation.walkthrough: In music F means forte (loud) and P means piano (soft), so 'softening' the top of FLAN turns its F into P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or intention, a worked-out notion.

clue.text: Outstanding feature of Cinders' sisters

parts.note: Cinderella's stepsisters are the Ugly Sisters of pantomime, known mainly for their looks

explanation.surface: Praise for Cinderella's sisters' most striking quality.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime Cinderella's stepsisters are 'the Ugly Sisters', so their most notable trait is plainness; 'Outstanding' sounds complimentary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ugly Sisters are defined by their unattractiveness, their most noticeable quality.

clue.text: Provides opportunities

definitions.meaning: provides here means causes or brings about
opportunities means favourable times or chances

explanation.surface: Someone supplies openings.
explanation.definitionFit: To occasion is to bring about or give rise to something; occasions are also chances or suitable times.

clue.text: Got into very hot water

parts.note: read literally, someone has been plunged into near-boiling liquid, not in trouble

explanation.surface: Someone landed in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'in hot water' means in trouble; read literally, being put in very hot water burns the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To be scalded is to be burnt by hot liquid or steam.

clue.text: It was left to sailors in the old days

definitions.text: It was left to sailors in the old days

parts.words: It was left to sailors in the old days
parts.note: an old seafaring word for the left-hand side of a ship, later replaced by port

explanation.surface: Something was bequeathed to seamen long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left to' reads like a bequest, but it means 'meant left' for old sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the obsolete nautical term for port, the left side of a vessel facing forward.

clue.text: Confronted by two consecutive letters rubbed out

parts.note: E and F come one after the other in the alphabet
confronted means faced

explanation.surface: Faced with a couple of adjacent letters that have been erased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word placing the two letters alongside FACED.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to wipe out or erase a mark.

clue.text: Small mark left bloodsucker is only a trifle

definitions.meaning: the small red spot left behind by a parasitic insect's bite
a figurative minor irritation or trivial matter

explanation.surface: A flea's tiny bite is nothing serious.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea's bite leaves a little red spot, and figuratively such a bite means a minor nuisance.

clue.text: Female Russian artisan in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the word artisan is upset and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Russian woman craftsman finds herself in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges ARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or a Russian empress.

clue.text: Fancies current account charges

parts.note: C/A is the banking abbreviation for a current account
charges are prices

explanation.surface: A bank's current account fees are imaginary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current account' reads as banking talk, and banks do write it C/A.
explanation.definitionFit: Caprices are whims, sudden notions or impulses.

clue.text: Roman statesman, one interested in jazz-circle?

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz fan
the letter O has the shape of a circle

explanation.surface: A Roman politician who is a member of a jazz club.
explanation.walkthrough: In jazz slang a 'cat' is an enthusiast. Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder was a famous Roman politician and censor.

clue.text: Sore from damaging London statue

indicators.note: damaging means the word sore is broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A London monument has been hurt by vandalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaging' rearranges SORE. The statue atop the Shaftesbury Memorial in Piccadilly Circus is popularly called Eros.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure in Piccadilly Circus is widely known by the name of the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Start, or I'll take an alcoholic drink

parts.note: taken as written
the I of I'll supplies the letter, the 'll being part of the link
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone threatens to begin drinking spirits unless something happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take an' is link material joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is a beginning or source.

clue.text: Enter unusual items in an auction, maybe

indicators.note: unusual signals that the word enter is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone puts strange lots up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ENTER. Treen is old turned wooden household ware, often sold at antiques auctions.
explanation.definitionFit: Treen means small wooden domestic objects, typical lots in antique sales.

clue.text: Pull no punches when greeting a solicitor

parts.note: hi is a greeting
a tout solicits custom, so a solicitor in that sense

explanation.surface: Speak frankly when saying hello to a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer but here is one who solicits business, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit out is to attack forcefully, holding nothing back.

clue.text: Jewish teacher's attempt at being an incurably inferior player in a game

definitions.text: being an incurably inferior player in a game

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A rabbi tries his hand and proves hopeless at a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a 'rabbit' is a poor player at a game such as cricket or tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit is British slang for a hopeless player, so the abstract noun is the state of being one.

clue.text: Poles are to set a trap

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Polish people are laying a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland but means the magnetic poles S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a noose or device for catching animals.

clue.text: Aunt upset, worn out, ready for a bath

indicators.note: upset means the word aunt is knocked into a new order

parts.note: worn out means tired

explanation.surface: An aunt is cross and exhausted before taking a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges AUNT into UNAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undressed, without clothing, is the state needed to step into a bath.
